blog_summary: The blog post discusses the paper 'DéjàVu: A map of code duplicates on GitHub' from OOPSLA '17, which analyzes duplication in 4.5 million GitHub projects. The authors found that 82% of files have duplicates elsewhere in GitHub, though this is largely due to trivial files and dependency management practices. The study defines three levels of duplication: exact file hashes, token hashes (minor changes), and near-duplicates (80% token similarity via SourcererCC). JavaScript exhibits the highest duplication (94% file-level clones), primarily due to NPM dependencies being committed to repositories. The paper also explores project-level duplication and identifies auto-generated code and popular frameworks as major contributors to duplication. The authors propose their 'clone map' as a tool to help researchers curate non-duplicate samples for studies.
paper_title: DéjàVu: A map of code duplicates on GitHub
